title: Endpoint SLO anchoring and graded fallback policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose:
Define a canonical approach for anchoring SLOs to endpoint/model behavioral curves and implement a graded fallback policy (soft degrade -> hard degrade -> regional ejection) that ties to error budget burn. This ticket codifies SLI definitions per endpoint and model variant, precise error budget math, clear circuit-breaker thresholds for live traffic, and an operational runbook for gradual degradation and automated remediation.

Background and motivation:
We currently have many ad-hoc SLOs and a handful of circuit-breaker rules that vary by team and model. This causes inconsistent behavior during bursts and cross-region incidents: some routes eject too early, others never degrade until tail latency spikes produce customer-visible failures. We need a reproducible, testable policy so that: 1) SLOs are comparable across endpoints; 2) fallback actions are predictable; 3) error budget exhaustion triggers are actionable and safe for production traffic; and 4) operators can reason about cost vs quality tradeoffs for each endpoint/model.

Scope (what this ticket will deliver):
- Canonical SLI definitions for generation/chat (latency P95, P99, and quality-sensitive request success), embeddings (throughput & failure rate), and reranking (precision-at-K hooks). These will be expressed in measurement queries for Prometheus and tracing spans.
- Error budget formula and burn-rate window defaults (1d burn-window for high-traffic routes, 7d for low-traffic).
- Graded fallback policy tied to both SLO burn and instantaneous capacity signals: three tiers (Tier A: soft degrade – reduce max tokens / switch to cached prefix; Tier B: hard degrade – route to quantized lower-cost variant with quality score metadata; Tier C: regional ejection – shift traffic to alternate region / model variant).
- Circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis: how many 5xx/latency violations in a rolling window trigger each tier, and the cooldown/backoff strategy.
- Operational runbook: steps for on-call, dashboards to consult, rollback procedures, and post-incident follow-up requirements.
- Test plan for unit/integration tests, chaos scenarios, and staged rollout requirements for both Hosted and Dedicated customers.

Non-goals:
- Changes to billing model or pricing.
- Model-level quality remediation (e.g., retraining). We will only attach quality signals for downstream ops and rollback logic.

Unique considerations: 
- Tenant-aware SLOs: endpoints with higher-paying tenants will be allowed separate error budget slices (future follow-up). For this initial policy we prioritize per-endpoint/model SLOs with optional label-based overrides.
- Private (VPC) deployments: the policy must be implementable without central control-plane dependencies; fallback logic should run in local control-plane agents when possible.

Deliverables (artifact list):
- SLI & SLO reference document (Markdown) with Prometheus query examples and sampling guidance.
- Circuit-breaker config template and runtime knobs in the routing layer.
- Runbook (ops playbook) with step-by-step escalation and dashboards links.
- Test harness additions (integration tests and synthetic chaos scenarios).
acceptance_criteria: Published SLI reference doc with concrete Prometheus/trace queries for at least three representative endpoints (chat-generate, embeddings, rerank)
Error budget formula documented with sample calculations for a high-traffic and low-traffic endpoint
Routing layer accepts a JSON circuit-breaker config and can execute three-tier fallback actions in a staging environment
Runbook validated with a simulated SLO burn exercise and on-call sign-off
Automated tests simulate traffic patterns that trigger each fallback tier and assert traffic routing and metadata tags are correct
Rollout plan approved and can be toggled per-region and per-customer tier
notes: Anchor SLOs to measurable outcome: prefer availability-style SLI (successful candidate generation within latency bound) instead of app-level subjective quality metrics
Use adaptive burn-window sizing: endpoints with <100 req/day use 7d window to avoid noisy burn signals
Integrate quality-exposed metadata (quality_score) on responses to allow safe fallbacks to lower-cost variants while tracking customer-visible quality delta
technical_decisions: SLI definitions will use P95 latency and a binary success criteria: response completes without server-side errors and returns >threshold tokens when applicable
Default error budget: 99.9% availability target (monthly) unless endpoint declares a stricter contract
Three-tier fallback chosen to give gradual degradation and preserve customer experience while protecting core capacity
monitoring_and_alerts: Primary alert: error budget burn-rate > 4x expected for 30m -> notify SRE and trigger automated first-tier fallback
Secondary alert: sustained P99 latency breach for 5m after soft degrade -> escalate to hard degrade
Tertiary alert: cross-region capacity mismatch detected + error budget exhausted -> flag for regional ejection and page on-call
rollout_plan: Implement feature flags for circuit-breaker configs; default OFF in prod
Stage rollout: 1) internal canaries (staging) 2) small set of non-critical endpoints in prod 3) broad rollout by traffic class
Run a simulated SLO burn drill over a 48h window with SRE and product + record outcome
